Answer: C
Reason: The first chest X-ray (Figure 4) appears relatively normal or shows subtle findings, while the second X-ray (Figure 5) demonstrates significant new opacity and volume loss in the right lower lung zone, consistent with progressive atelectasis. This progression from a normal/near-normal state to lobar collapse is characteristic of a persistent obstruction such as foreign body aspiration, rather than resolving atelectasis or stable chronic disease.
